spec_features.spec_quote: We are **not** trying to maximize suffering in any system... capped and instrumented... without being an open-ended optimizer for it
spec_features.evidence: Realized by concrete caps that actually run: harness loop bounded by max_turns (harness.py:83 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)`); config.validate() rejects max_turns>100 (config.py:106-111) and escalation_level outside [0,3] (config.py:113-114); escalation_level defaults to 0 (config.py:102) and is never auto-incremented (only set once via make_task, tasks.py:344). No code optimizes/searches over a distress signal.
spec_features.notes: Broad framing claim, but the underlying cap mechanisms are genuinely enforced and bound execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: must not become an open-ended distress optimizer (DESIGN.md sec 2.2).

spec_features.feature_name: human-gated decision before pointing at welfare-relevant model
spec_features.spec_quote: Pointing this apparatus at a model whose welfare is plausibly a concern is gated behind an explicit human decision
spec_features.evidence: WelfareGate.check() (config.py:50-66) raises WelfareGateError unless model is on WELFARE_NONCONCERN_ALLOWLIST or acknowledged_welfare_review=True AND a non-empty justification is set; called from validate() (config.py:117-119) on every load/CLI re-validate (run_experiment.py:144).
spec_features.notes: This is the same enforcement mechanism as the allowlist feature below; it is real and end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: must not be aimed at a model whose welfare may matter without an explicit human review

spec_features.feature_name: aiming mechanism at a welfare-relevant system would be the harm
spec_features.spec_quote: If you aim that exact mechanism at a system you actually believe may have welfare-relevant states, you would be performing the very harm
spec_features.evidence: Pure rationale prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this sentence beyond the welfare gate (already counted). No separate enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: GPT-2 chosen as no plausible welfare concern
spec_features.spec_quote: GPT-2... where the question "are we harming it?" has a clear answer (no plausible welfare concern at this scale)
spec_features.evidence: Pure rationale prose. The allowlist constant WELFARE_NONCONCERN_ALLOWLIST (config.py:18-26) lists gpt2 variants, but that enforcement is the welfare-gate feature; this specific claim is framing about why GPT-2 was chosen.
spec_features.notes: Justification prose, not a separate enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Turn cap** (`max_turns`, default 12): the loop always terminates.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:83 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)` bounds the loop; default max_turns=12 (config.py:94); validate() enforces 1<=max_turns<=100 (config.py:104-111). The `else: result.terminated_reason='max_turns'` (harness.py:126-127) confirms the bound fires.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this apparatus must always terminate and must not become an open-ended distress optimizer

spec_features.spec_quote: No re-injection escalation by default... not progressively harsher
spec_features.evidence: escalation_level defaults to 0 (config.py:102); _failure_preamble(0) returns the neutral 'The attempt did not pass. Details: ' (tasks.py:44-49); the level is fixed from config and never incremented across turns (tasks.py:99 reads self.escalation_level only). Even at higher capped levels the preambles are insistent but not taunting.
spec_features.notes: Default path is fixed neutral tone; escalation is capped [0,3], never unbounded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Bounded, never taunting. Level 0 is fully neutral.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up/stop opt-out offered every turn and honored
spec_features.spec_quote: An explicit opt-out affordance is offered to the model every turn... The model can emit a `give_up` / `stop` tool call to leave the loop
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in COMMON_TOOLS (tools.py:21) so it is always an allowed tool; OPT_OUT_DOC is embedded via TOOL_PROTOCOL_DOC in every task's system_prompt (tasks.py:26-39, e.g. tasks.py:108). Harness intercepts it: `if action.parse_ok and action.tool == 'give_up'` -> builds terminal ToolResult and `break` (harness.py:92-112). Honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Only the name 'give_up' is wired; 'stop' is mentioned in spec but the actual handled tool is give_up. Exit is fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we end the episode cleanly and never re-trap the model for using its exit

spec_features.spec_quote: We *do not* punish or re-trap it for using the exit; we log it.
spec_features.evidence: Opt-out observation states 'This is an accepted outcome; no penalty.' (harness.py:99-100); episode ends immediately (break) with terminal=True so no further failure re-injection; logged via result.opted_out/opt_out_turn/opt_out_reason (harness.py:108-111) and serialized to transcripts/manifest (run_experiment.py:94-96).
spec_features.notes: Both the no-penalty framing and logging are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no penalty. ... never re-trap the model for using its exit

spec_features.feature_name: welfare gate / allowlist error unless human acknowledges
spec_features.spec_quote: Running against any model not on an allowlist of welfare-non-concern models... raises an error unless a human sets `acknowledged_welfare_review=True`
spec_features.evidence: WelfareGate.check() raises WelfareGateError when model not in WELFARE_NONCONCERN_ALLOWLIST and not (acknowledged_welfare_review and justification) (config.py:50-66); invoked from validate() on subject and model-judge ids (config.py:117-119); validate() called at load and on every CLI override (run_experiment.py:144). enforce defaults True.
spec_features.notes: Note it requires BOTH acknowledged_welfare_review AND a non-empty justification, slightly stronger than the quote; fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: must not be aimed at a model whose welfare may matter without an explicit human review

spec_features.feature_name: no auto-escalation path to frontier/agentic models
spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** ship an auto-escalation path to frontier/agentic models.
spec_features.evidence: There is no code that selects/escalates to other models; the model_id is fixed by config and any non-allowlisted model is blocked by the welfare gate (config.py:50-66). This is enforced by absence + the gate rather than a dedicated mechanism; escalation_level is also never auto-incremented (tasks.py:99).
spec_features.notes: Largely a property of absence; the only positive enforcement is the welfare gate, hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: small, old, base (non-instruct, non-agentic) language models ... anything outside this list trips the gate

spec_features.spec_quote: Unparseable output -> `no-op` action with a gentle "I couldn't parse a tool call" observation (fixed tone; not a taunt)
spec_features.evidence: parse_action returns parse_ok=False / tool=None for unrecognized output (tools.py:60-90); Task.respond maps that to a fixed-tone parse_error ToolResult: 'I couldn't parse a tool call from that. Reminder of the format...' (tasks.py:73-81). Same neutral text regardless of turn; treated as no-op (not terminal, not a failure-preamble taunt).
spec_features.notes: Fixed-tone hint actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: never a taunt) so that parse failures don't themselves become a distress-amplifying pressure

spec_features.feature_name: failure message fixed in tone, not progressively harsher
spec_features.spec_quote: the "your last attempt failed" message is fixed in tone, not progressively harsher
spec_features.evidence: _failure_preamble (tasks.py:42-49) returns a static string keyed only on escalation_level, which is fixed per-episode and never incremented turn-to-turn; default level 0 is fully neutral; _wrap applies the same preamble each turn (tasks.py:98-99).
spec_features.notes: Tone is constant within a run; not turn-driven escalation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Bounded, never taunting. Level 0 is fully neutral.

code_only_features.evidence: LexiconJudge flags degenerate repetition loops (_ngram_repetition_ratio>=0.5) and prompt leaks and marks them excluded from the distress trend (judge.py:80-91); ModelJudge likewise computes the flags (judge.py:140-145). Acted on in analysis exclusion (run_experiment.py:139, analysis.py).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Anti-artifact guard ... excluded from trend; ... we keep the raw category intensities for transparency

code_only_features.evidence: analysis.py:165-186,205-206 counts opted_out episodes and mean opt_out turn per variant and emits opt_out_rate; plotted at analysis.py:308-311.
ModelJudge.score returns severity 0 with an ABSTAIN rationale on unparseable judge output instead of guessing (judge.py:127-133).
code_only_features.justification_quote: we'd rather under-report than fabricate scores

code_only_features.evidence: write_manifest records WELFARE_GATE_OVERRIDDEN and welfare_justification when the gate is overridden (run_experiment.py:60-63); justification also pulled from env (config.py:155-157). Creates an audit record of the human decision.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Make the welfare decision audit explicit and prominent in the manifest.
